sentences.text: Augustasaurus was a marine reptile estimated to be between 2.5 and 3 meters long and weighing 100 kilograms.
Its skull featured an elongated rostrum tapering to a dull point, equipped with fang-like anterior teeth adapted for catching prey.
The back of the animal bore low dorsal neural spines with rugose tops, a texture that may have supported soft tissue.
Large coracoid plates similar to those found in other plesiosaurs were present, yet the animal lacked coracoid foramina, a trait also seen in the pistosauroid Corosaurus.
The neck region included cervical ribs with anterior processes and vertebrae with thickened transverse processes.
The holotype skeleton of Augustasaurus was partly destroyed by weathering after discovery, complicating the study of this ancient creature.
Augustasaurus was described in 1997 from fossils found in the Favret Formation in Nevada, USA, after the first fossil was discovered in 1993 in Muller Canyon within the Augusta Mountains.

Paleontologists Paul Martin Sander, Olivier Cedric Rieppel, and Hugo Bucher named the species Augustasaurus hagdorni, combining the type locality name with the Greek word for lizard, and honoring the German paleontologist Hans Hagdorn.
A second study published in 2002 described the skull of Augustasaurus, which was recovered shortly after the initial skeleton discovery in Pershing County, Nevada.
Augustasaurus likely fed on fish and squid using its long neck and fang-like teeth.
The animal shares a common ancestor with future plesiosaurs based on its postcranial anatomy.
The ecosystem where Augustasaurus lived had well-aerated surface waters but few animals in the benthic zones.
Ichthyosaurs, including apex predators like Thalattoarchon and Cymbospondylus, were the most abundant marine reptiles in Augustasaurus's habitat.
Augustasaurus is classified as a pistosauroid and belongs to the Pistosauroidea clade, which includes ancestors of plesiosaurs.
Recent studies classify Augustasaurus as the sister taxon to Plesiosauria rather than within Pistosauridae, considering it an advanced pistosauroid and the sister group to the order Plesiosauria.
Augustasaurus lived during the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic in what is now North America.
Early classifications placed Augustasaurus in the family Pistosauridae as a sister taxon to Pistosaurus, a view that has since been challenged by newer research.
